claims.text: The baseline is an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a conventional metal substrate.
The as-deposited coating has a relatively coarse microstructure.
The as-deposited coating has a heterogeneous microstructure.
The as-deposited coating has a nonuniform oxide distribution.
Controlled post-deposition annealing will refine the coating's grain structure.
The annealed coating will have a nanocrystalline microstructure.
Grain refinement will increase grain-boundary density.
Increased grain-boundary density will promote formation of a uniform protective oxide layer.
Increased grain-boundary area will restrict dislocation motion through grain-boundary pinning.
Increased grain-boundary area will facilitate rapid oxide-film formation during sliding.
Increased grain-boundary area will facilitate spatially uniform oxide-film formation during sliding.
The combined dislocation restriction and protective oxide film will lower the wear rate.
The combined dislocation restriction and protective oxide film will reduce localized plastic deformation.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, the annealed coating will exhibit a lower wear rate during high-temperature sliding.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, the annealed coating will exhibit less microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding.
The predicted effects are expected in an oxidizing sliding environment at approximately 500–800 °C, where oxidation, diffusion, and dislocation processes are active.
The predicted effects may not hold at lower temperatures or in atmospheres that do not support oxide formation.
A lack of statistically significant reductions in both wear rate and microscopic deformation in the annealed group is designated as a falsifying result.
